function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty dessert, or a last‑minute pick‑up: | Category | What it offers | How to find it | |----------|----------------|----------------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for birthdays, weddings, or just a treat | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps, Yelp, or Apple Maps. Look at photos, read recent reviews, and call ahead to confirm availability and delivery options. | | **Online grocery & delivery services** | Ready‑to‑eat cakes from big chains (e.g., Costco, Walmart), plus local bakery picks delivered to your door | • **Instacart** – choose a local store or independent bakery.
• **Amazon Fresh** – wide selection of pre‑baked cakes and desserts.
• **Shipt** – similar to Instacart, often includes local shops. | | **Food‑delivery apps** | Cakes from restaurants, cafés, and specialty shops; convenient for quick orders | • **Uber Eats** – many local bakeries and cafés list their cakes here.
• **DoorDash** – same as above, plus some “food truck” options.
• **Postmates** – good for niche or artisanal cakes. | | **Specialty cake sites** | Custom designs, themed cakes, or high‑end pastries | • **Bakeology** – custom cakes, cupcakes, and wedding cakes.
• **Goldbelly** – regional specialties (think New York cheesecake, Southern pecan pie).
• **Etsy** – handmade cakes from independent bakers worldwide. | | **Convenience stores & supermarkets** | Pre‑packaged cakes, sheet cakes, and boxed mixes | • **7‑Eleven**, **Circle K**, **Walmart**, **Target** – all carry ready‑to‑eat cakes. | | **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (great for gifts or regular treats) | • **The Cake Club** – monthly cake subscription.
• **Baker’s Dozen** – artisanal cake box delivered quarterly. | ### Tips for ordering 1. **Check delivery windows** – especially for custom cakes, they may need a few days’ notice. 2. **Read recent reviews** – look for comments about freshness, taste, and packaging. 3. **Ask about shipping** – if you’re ordering online, confirm how the cake will be insulated and whether it arrives on time. 4. **Compare prices** – sometimes a local bakery will offer better quality for a comparable price, even after adding delivery fees. If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries or delivery partners that serve your area!
